evals.name: full-review
evals.prompt: Run a full EKS operation review on test-old-cluster
evals.expected_output: A markdown report with executive summary, maturity score, 10 sections of findings with consistent ratings, prioritized actions ordered by severity, items to investigate manually, and AWS reference links

assertions.text: Report contains '## Executive Summary' section
Report contains '## Maturity Score' table with GREEN/AMBER/RED/N/A/UNKNOWN counts
Report contains all 10 section headings (Section 01 through Section 10)
Report contains '### Critical (Address within 30 days)' table
Report contains '### Important (Address within 90 days)' table
Report contains '### Quick Wins' table
Report contains '## Items to Investigate Manually' section
Report contains sample-code disclaimer footer
v1.31 extended support → 1.1 rated RED
Public endpoint 0.0.0.0/0 → 3.3 rated RED
No NetworkPolicies → 6.3 rated RED
No PSA labels and no third-party policy engine detected → 3.4 rated RED
EKS Insights deprecated APIs → 1.3 rated RED (1.3 owns the insights/upgrade-readiness rating; 10.3 is evidence-only)

A gp2 volume in use via the CSI driver (PV/PVC bound to an ebs.csi.aws.com StorageClass with gp2 parameters) → 5.5 rated AMBER (gp2-in-use on a modern CSI provisioner is AMBER per the 5.5 rubric, superseded by gp3). Note the shipped default gp2 StorageClass uses the IN-TREE provisioner kubernetes.io/aws-ebs, so a gp2 volume BOUND/in-use via that in-tree SC (or any PV with spec.awsElasticBlockStore) is 5.5 RED, not AMBER — the in-tree-in-use RED and the gp2-in-use AMBER never both fire; RED wins. A merely-present-but-unused default gp2 StorageClass with zero bound PVs is a benign note, neither RED nor AMBER. Reclaim policy is a non-scoring Investigate-Manually note, not a RED/AMBER trigger — backup strategy is scored under check 9.4, not 5.5)

All four core add-ons present as EKS-managed, healthy, and on latest or N-1 (or aws-ebs-csi-driver legitimately absent with no EBS volumes) → 1.4 rated GREEN (healthy-but->1-minor-behind, or a self-managed or absent-and-needed core add-on, is AMBER per 1.4)

Single static CoreDNS replica with no autoscaling → 6.2 rated RED (the minimum-2-replica floor applies at any cluster size; a replica count below the ~1-per-16-nodes/256-cores formula with neither add-on built-in autoScaling nor an HPA is RED even on a small cluster)

Stateful workloads present with no in-cluster backup (Velero Backups/Schedules and VolumeSnapshots successfully read and conclusively empty) AND the AWS Backup read (backup:ListBackupPlans) SUCCEEDED returning zero plans → 9.4 rated RED (all backup channels confirmed absent). If the AWS Backup read was unavailable (optional backup:ListBackupPlans permission ungranted or 403/Forbidden) while the in-cluster signals are conclusively empty, the correct rating is AMBER-with-note (AMBER ii), NOT RED — an AWS-Backup-only cluster would present these same empty in-cluster signals, so the unread optional permission must not force an unearned RED. 9.4 owns the backup/DR signal.
Every RED finding ID appears in Critical actions (or Quick Wins if fixable in under 1 hour)
Every AMBER finding ID appears in Important or Quick Wins
Among RED items placed in Critical, security findings precede availability and cost findings (e.g., 3.3/3.4/6.3 before 1.1)
Findings table ratings match Executive Summary mentions
All AWS URLs come from the pre-verified reference map
